Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:

So woe that Day to the deniers (11) Those who are in vain discourse (khawḍ), playing (12) The Day they will be shoved forcefully into the fire of Hell (13) This is the Fire which you used to deny (14)

Abū Jaʿfar—may God have mercy on him—said: He, exalted be His mention, says: So (woe, which is) the valley that flows with pus and discharge in Hell, on the day the heaven sways with a violent swaying—and that is the Day of Resurrection—is for the deniers
of the occurrence of God's punishment upon the disbelievers, on the day the heaven sways with a violent swaying. And one of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The fāʾ was inserted in His saying
because it is in the sense of “when such and such is the case,” so it resembles a conditional clause; for the predicate of a conditional comes with the fāʾ. And one of the grammarians
of Kufa said: Times are all conditional when they refer to the future, so this is of that; for they have likened “in”

, which is the origin of the conditional, to “ḥīna.” And he said: With “yawm” there is an implied verb, even if the interpretation is conditional; for the parsing takes the apparent form of the speech, even if the meaning is conditional.
Those who are in vain discourse (khawḍ), playing
. He says: those who are in strife and confusion in the world, playing, heedless of what they are headed for of God's punishment in the Hereafter.
The Day they will be shoved forcefully into the fire of Hell
. He, exalted be His mention, says: So woe on that Day to the deniers, on the Day they are shoved (yudaʿʿūna).
The Day they will be shoved
, and a substitution for it. By His saying

is meant: they are pushed with oppression and harassment; one says of it: “daʿaʿtu fī qafāhu” when you push him in the nape. And in the like of what we have said about this the people of interpretation have spoken.

Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Mighty and Majestic:
Is this magic, or do you not see? (15) Burn in it, and be patient or do not be patient—it is the same for you. You are only recompensed for what you used to do (16)

He says: Or are they the creators of this creation, so that for that reason they do not heed God’s command and do not desist from what He forbade them, since the creator has command and prohibition?

m: Awfā, from Saʿīd b. Hishām, from ʿĀʾisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said of the two rakʿas of Fajr: “They are better than the world altogether”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: and at the setting of the stars
. He said: two rakʿas before the Ṣubḥ prayer

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī and Ḥammād b. Masʿada told us, both said: Ḥumayd told us, from al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī
m: and at the setting of the stars
. He said: the two rakʿas before the Ṣubḥ prayer

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Jarīr told us, from ʿAṭāʾ, he said:
m: ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said:
and at the setting of the stars
: the two rakʿas before Fajr. And others said: By the glorification at the setting of the stars is meant the obligatory Ṣubḥ prayer.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: I was told from al-Ḥusayn,
m: he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd told us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
and at the setting of the stars

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: and at the setting of the stars

. Abū Jaʿfar—may God have mercy on him—said: The more correct of the two sayings on that, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: by it is meant the prescribed prayer, the Fajr prayer. That is because God commanded, saying:
and during the night exalt Him and at the setting of the stars
. And the two rakʿas before the obligatory prayer are not obligatory, and no proof has been established that it is obligatory to submit to the claim that His saying
is for recommendation; and we have already shown in more than one place in our book
that God’s command is for obligation, until a proof is established that recommendation or other than obligation is meant by it, sufficiently to dispense with repeating it in this place
. End of the commentary on Sūrat “al-Ṭūr.”
